# Brief — watercolor

**Status:** FROZEN — S1b pilot brief. Do not edit after scaffolding.
**Director:** Paper Studio, creative owner
**Frozen:** 2026-10-26
**Style id:** watercolor

This is a style brief, not a content brief. It describes the look for a small
garden wedding invitation film and for a song/memory film. Names, dates and
places arrive later in a content brief; the style never invents them.

## 1. Occasion and audience

A garden wedding invitation film for a small guest list, watched on a phone and
projected at the reception. A second use is a song/memory film for a creator.
The audience is close to the people in the film; they will watch it once, and
they will notice whether it feels hand-made or manufactured.

## 2. Story in one sentence

A painted field journal of a day: the garden, the table, the weather, and the
small things someone would want to remember.

## 3. Cast and faces

No on-camera cast and no photographic likeness. The couple appears as names, a
monogram and painted motifs. Painted plants, objects and small animals carry the
life of the film. No talking heads, no hands arranging objects, no footage of
the event itself.

## 4. Shape and length

Three shapes: a 1:1 journal page, eight shots, 45 seconds; a 16:9 handscroll,
one continuous walk, four shots, 45 seconds; a 9:16 vertical page, six shots,
30 seconds for the creator cut. The 1:1 page is the primary proof. The page
shapes use the page contracts — title, specimen, quote, mist, close — and may
repeat a page contract. The handscroll adds the walk. The walk's twelve-second
minimum belongs to the 45-second scroll, not the 30-second page.

## 5. Feeling

Calm, curious, hand-made. A page from a naturalist's field journal: precise
enough to trust, loose enough to feel painted. It should feel like someone
looked closely and then wrote a note in the margin.

## 6. Anti-feeling

Never a greeting card. Never a children's picture book. Never a vector
illustration with a watercolour texture laid on top. Never an ink-wash pastiche.
Never a glossy advert. If it starts to feel cute, rustic-craft or software-made,
it has failed.

## 7. Material and palette

Warm cotton paper, transparent pigment, one vermilion accent, a second petal or
ochre hue, and a deeper wash made by more passes rather than a darker tube colour. At most five pigments in one frame. Paper is the white.
No pure white paint, no cast shadow, no gloss, no foil, no gold, no metallic
sheen, no opaque flat fill.

## 8. Type and words

Cormorant Garamond italic for titles, Cormorant regular for subtitles, body and
quotes, Caveat for hand notes, IBM Plex Mono for measured labels. Sixteen words
maximum per content slot; fourteen pixels minimum at 390 px width. At 9:16,
recompose the page: display 44 px, body 24 px, caption 24 px, label 14 px,
monogram 18 px; keep the title in the left column and the arch on the right. The
scale is authored for a 390 px-wide page; larger frames scale proportionally. The
fourteen-pixel floor stays. Latin script only for this pilot. No all-caps
paragraphs, no text over the subject, no fourth family.

## 9. Motion and pace

Things paint themselves in, structure before detail. A long lateral pan for the
walk; a slow push-in for a specimen; a brush-edge wipe between plates; a page
turn between journal pages; a silent paper-coloured mist to erase; a hold at the
close. No hard cuts, no dissolves, no bounce, no overshoot, no camera shake.
Paint-in speed is 1.2 s or 1.8 s per painted form; a specimen is the reference,
and a quote's object paints in by the same rule. The director chooses at review.

## 10. Sound

Felt piano, fingerpicked guitar, light strings, glockenspiel or kalimba; no
drums. Foley from the scene's matter: paper brush rustle, pencil scratch, a soft
page turn, a quiet stamp thump. Silence is a colour: music is out from the mist
through the close, paper and room only; one quiet stamp thump is allowed at the
close. Voice optional, warm and unhurried. The style carries no audio files;
music and voice are cleared per film. Delivery loudness belongs to the format.

## 11. Refusals

No vector outline. No vector shape filled with a watercolour texture. No pure
white paint. No opaque flat fill. No impasto. No calligraphic gesture. No cast
shadow. No gloss, foil or gold. No hard cut. No dissolve. No more than five
pigments in a frame. No text over the subject. No photographic likeness. No
stock-photo smiles. No children's-book cuteness. No ink-wash pastiche. Out of
scope: photo-led weddings, non-Latin scripts, 3D, talking heads, trend edits.

## 12. Tier and proof

Signature tier. Proven by `style:check` REVIEWABLE with no hard failures; a 2×2
resolve across two briefs and two formats; a sealed blind application at 30 s,
9:16, six shots with the pack unchanged; the card at 900×700 and on a 390 px
phone; and three post-build critics at 9/10 GO. Proof frames: title, specimen and
close at 1:1, 16:9 and 9:16. No renderer and no video in S1b.
